title.en: Network security: what to protect, and the basics of cryptography
title.zh: 网络安全入门：要保护什么，密码学基础

description.en: Tell apart the five things security must protect, understand the encryption model and Kerckhoffs's principle, and work through shift, substitution, transposition and the one-time pad by hand.
description.zh: 分清安全要保护的五件事，看懂加密模型和柯克霍夫原则，并亲手算一遍移位、替换、换位和一次性密码本。

name.en: The five basic properties of network security
name.zh: 网络安全的五个基本性质 (security properties)

name.en: Man-in-the-middle attack and DDoS: two incidents
name.zh: 中间人攻击与 DDoS：两个事件 (man-in-the-middle attack, DDoS)
各层协议里的安全措施 (security at every layer)

name.en: The encryption model: plaintext, ciphertext and key
name.zh: 加密模型：明文、密文与密钥 (plaintext, ciphertext, key)

name.en: Kerckhoffs's principle and the key space
name.zh: 柯克霍夫原则与密钥空间 (Kerckhoff's principle, key space)

name.en: Three classical ideas: shift, substitution and transposition
name.zh: 三种经典思路：移位、替换与换位 (substitution and transposition ciphers)
一次性密码本与异或 (one-time pad, XOR)

description.en: Thinking that once something is encrypted, everything is fine. Encryption only covers confidentiality; the content can still be altered (integrity), and the other party may be an impostor (authentication).
description.zh: 以为加密了就万事大吉。加密只管机密性，内容仍可能被改（完整性），对方也可能是冒充的（认证）。

description.en: Confusing authentication with non-repudiation. Authentication confirms who the other party is right now; non-repudiation means being able to prove to a third party afterwards that a message came from a given person, which takes a signature.
description.zh: 把认证和不可否认性混为一谈。认证是当下确认对方是谁；不可否认性是事后能向第三方证明这条消息出自某人，要靠签名。

description.en: Thinking DDoS is there to steal data. DDoS reads and changes nothing; it just exhausts resources, and what it damages is availability.
description.zh: 以为 DDoS 是来偷数据的。DDoS 不读也不改任何内容，只是把资源耗尽，破坏的是可用性。

description.en: Thinking security comes from keeping the algorithm secret. Kerckhoffs's principle: the algorithm is public, and only the key is kept secret.
description.zh: 以为算法保密才安全。柯克霍夫原则：算法公开，只有密钥保密。

description.en: Thinking one more key bit adds only a little work. Each extra bit doubles the work of a brute-force search.
description.zh: 以为密钥多一位，工作量只多一点。每多一位，暴力搜索的工作量翻倍。

description.en: Thinking a large enough key space means it cannot be broken. A substitution cipher has 26! possible tables, and brute-force search is impractical, but the statistical clue of letter frequency lets it be broken anyway.
description.zh: 以为密钥空间够大就一定破不了。替换密码有 26! 种表，暴力搜索不现实，但字母频率这条统计线索让它照样被破。

description.en: Thinking the key of a one-time pad can be reused. If the same key is used twice, XORing the two ciphertexts cancels the key, and information about the plaintexts leaks out.
description.zh: 以为一次性密码本的密钥可以重复用。重复用同一把密钥，两条密文异或后密钥抵消，明文的信息就漏出来了。

title.en: Not a word understood, yet the transfer was changed
title.zh: 一个字也没读懂，却改了转账

prompt.en: Xiao Ming sends the bank an encrypted transfer instruction: transfer 100 yuan. Someone intercepts it on the way and, though they cannot read the content at all, randomly alters a few bits, and the amount the bank decrypts becomes 10000 yuan. Which property has been broken here?
prompt.zh: 小明给银行发了一条加密的转账指令：转 100 元。有人在路上截下它，虽然完全读不懂内容，但胡乱改了其中几位，银行解出来的金额变成了 10000 元。这里哪一件事被破坏了？

label.en: Confidentiality: someone saw the content
label.zh: 机密性：内容被人看到了

feedback.en: The attacker did not understand a single word, so the content did not leak.
feedback.zh: 攻击者一个字也没读懂，内容并没有泄露。

label.en: Integrity: someone changed the content
label.zh: 完整性：内容被人改动了

feedback.en: Right. You can change something without reading it, and the bank still thinks Xiao Ming sent it.
feedback.zh: 对。读不懂也能改，改了银行还以为是小明发的。

label.en: Availability: the bank's system was brought down
label.zh: 可用性：银行系统被弄瘫了

feedback.en: The system carried on running as usual; it just received an altered instruction.
feedback.zh: 系统照常运行，只是收到了一条被改过的指令。

explain.en: Security is not only about keeping people from seeing. Keeping people from seeing (confidentiality) and keeping people from changing (integrity) are two different things. This lesson starts by separating the several things to be protected.
explain.zh: 安全不只是不让人看。不让人看（机密性）、不让人改（完整性）是两件不同的事。这一课先把要保护的几件事分清楚。

title.en: Five properties, each remembered with a scene
title.zh: 五个性质，各用一个场景记

text.en: Security protects five things. Each comes with a scene from campus:
text.zh: 安全要保护五件事。每一件配一个校园里的场景：

rows.en: Keeping unauthorised people from seeing it

rows.zh: 你的成绩单别人看不到

rows.en: The content has not been changed
The assignment the teacher receives is the very one you handed in, not swapped
rows.zh: 老师收到的作业就是你交的那份，没被换

rows.en: Systems and services are not knocked out
The website still opens the moment course selection opens
rows.zh: 选课开放那一刻，网站还能打开

rows.en: Confirming the other party holds valid credentials and is who they claim to be
rows.zh: 确认对方持有合法凭据，是他说的那个人

rows.en: The website confirms that it is you logging in, and you confirm the website is genuine
rows.zh: 网站确认登录的是你，你也确认网站是真的

rows.en: Being able to prove the content came from a named person, by means of a signature
rows.zh: 能证明内容出自某个具名的人，靠签名

rows.en: On an application you signed, you cannot later say you did not write it
rows.zh: 你签过字的申请，事后不能说不是你写的

text.en: Two pairs that are easy to mix up:
text.zh: 容易混的两对：

items.en: **Authentication and non-repudiation**: authentication confirms who the other party is right now, and matters only to you; non-repudiation means you can still prove to a third party (a teacher, a judge) afterwards who sent it.
items.zh: **认证和不可否认性**：认证是当下确认对方是谁，只对你自己有意义；不可否认性是事后还能向第三方（老师、法官）证明是谁发的。

items.en: **Integrity and authentication**: integrity asks whether the content was altered; authentication asks whether the other party is who they say they are. The content can be untouched while the sender is an impostor; the sender can be genuine while the content was altered on the way.
items.zh: **完整性和认证**：完整性问的是内容有没有被改；认证问的是对方是不是他说的那个人。内容原封不动，发信人也可能是冒充的；发信人是真的，内容也可能在路上被改。

title.en: Which one is it?
title.zh: 是哪一条

prompt.en: Classmate Xiao Hong sent the teacher an email saying “I request an extension”. Later she denied sending it. The teacher wants evidence that this email really came from Xiao Hong. Which property does the teacher need?
prompt.zh: 同学小红给老师发了一封邮件说“我申请延期”。后来她否认发过。老师想拿出证据，证明这封邮件确实出自小红。老师需要的是哪个性质？

label.en: Confidentiality
label.zh: 机密性

feedback.en: Confidentiality is about keeping others from seeing the content, and has nothing to do with being able to prove who sent it.
feedback.zh: 机密性是不让别人看到内容，和能不能证明谁发的无关。

label.en: Authentication
label.zh: 认证

feedback.en: Authentication confirms who the other party is at the time of sending, which guarantees only that moment; proving it to a third party afterwards takes something stronger.
feedback.zh: 认证是发信时确认对方是谁，保证的是当时那一刻；事后向第三方证明还需要更强的东西。

label.en: Integrity
label.zh: 完整性

feedback.en: Integrity only shows the content has not been changed, not who wrote it.
feedback.zh: 完整性只说明内容没被改，不能说明是谁写的。

label.en: Non-repudiation
label.zh: 不可否认性

feedback.en: Right. To prove to a third party that the content came from a named person takes a signature, so that person cannot deny it.
feedback.zh: 对。要能向第三方证明这条内容出自具名的人，靠签名，对方不能抵赖。

explain.en: “Cannot deny it afterwards” is exactly non-repudiation. The digital signature in the next lesson is designed for it.
explain.zh: “事后不能抵赖”正是不可否认性。下一课的数字签名就是为它而设计的。

title.en: Equifax: where the man in the middle stands
title.zh: Equifax：中间人站在哪里

text.en: From March to July 2017, the credit reporting agency Equifax suffered a major incident, which the slides classify as a **man-in-the-middle attack**: the attacker intercepts the data sent between two parties and may also tamper with it. The attack went on for 75 days before it was discovered, about 143 million personal records may have been affected, and afterwards Equifax spent 1.4 billion US dollars upgrading its security.
text.zh: 2017 年 3 月到 7 月，信用报告机构 Equifax 出了一起大事故，课件把它归为**中间人攻击** (man-in-the-middle attack)：攻击者拦截两方之间发送的数据，还可能篡改它。攻击持续了 75 天才被发现，约 1.43 亿条个人记录可能受到影响，事后 Equifax 花了 14 亿美元升级安全。

title.en: Beyond the slides: how the incident actually happened
title.zh: 超出课件：这起事故实际是怎么发生的

body.en: The slides do not cover how Equifax was attacked. The public post-incident investigations usually trace the cause to a web application vulnerability that had not been patched in time, not a textbook man in the middle. What this page is meant to teach is what the position of “standing between two parties” lets you do, so the figure below draws the textbook man in the middle.
body.zh: 课件没有讲 Equifax 的攻击手法。公开的事后调查，通常把原因归到一个没有及时修补的网页应用漏洞，而不是教科书式的中间人。这一页要学的是“站在两方中间”这个位置能做什么，所以下图画的是教科书里的中间人。

text.en: Why does the man in the middle hurt three properties at once? Look at where he stands: Alice thinks she is talking to Bob, but is actually talking to Trudy.
text.zh: 中间人为什么同时伤到三个性质？看他站的位置：Alice 以为自己在和 Bob 说话，其实是在和 Trudy 说话。

svg.en: <svg viewBox='0 0 720 260' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif'><rect width='720' height='260' fill='#fafafa'/><g fill='#fff' stroke='#333' stroke-width='2'><rect x='20' y='60' width='110' height='60' rx='6'/><rect x='305' y='60' width='110' height='60' rx='6'/><rect x='590' y='60' width='110' height='60' rx='6'/></g><g fill='#222' font-size='16' text-anchor='middle'><text x='75' y='96'>Alice</text><text x='360' y='96'>Trudy</text><text x='645' y='96'>Bob</text></g><g stroke='#333' stroke-width='2'><path d='M130 90 H305'/><path d='M415 90 H590'/></g><g fill='#333'><path d='M305 90 l-9 -5 v10 z'/><path d='M590 90 l-9 -5 v10 z'/></g><g fill='#c0392b' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle'><text x='360' y='160'>Reads the content: confidentiality broken</text><text x='360' y='188'>Changes the content: integrity broken</text><text x='360' y='216'>Impersonates the other side: authentication broken</text></g><text x='360' y='244' font-size='14' fill='#555' text-anchor='middle'>All three fall at once</text></svg>
svg.zh: <svg viewBox='0 0 720 260' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' font-family='sans-serif'><rect width='720' height='260' fill='#fafafa'/><g fill='#fff' stroke='#333' stroke-width='2'><rect x='20' y='60' width='110' height='60' rx='6'/><rect x='305' y='60' width='110' height='60' rx='6'/><rect x='590' y='60' width='110' height='60' rx='6'/></g><g fill='#222' font-size='16' text-anchor='middle'><text x='75' y='96'>Alice</text><text x='360' y='96'>Trudy</text><text x='645' y='96'>Bob</text></g><g stroke='#333' stroke-width='2'><path d='M130 90 H305'/><path d='M415 90 H590'/></g><g fill='#333'><path d='M305 90 l-9 -5 v10 z'/><path d='M590 90 l-9 -5 v10 z'/></g><g fill='#c0392b' font-size='15' text-anchor='middle'><text x='360' y='160'>读到内容：机密性被破坏</text><text x='360' y='188'>改动内容：完整性被破坏</text><text x='360' y='216'>冒充对方：认证被破坏</text></g><text x='360' y='244' font-size='14' fill='#555' text-anchor='middle'>三条同时失守</text></svg>

alt.en: All data between Alice and Bob passes through Trudy in the middle, who can read it, change it and impersonate
alt.zh: Alice 和 Bob 之间的所有数据都经过中间的 Trudy，她可以读、改、冒充

caption.en: The man in the middle stands between the two parties

text.en: He can read, so confidentiality is broken; he can change, so integrity is broken; he impersonates each side to the other, so authentication is broken too. The three are three abilities that come from the same position.
text.zh: 他能读，机密性破；他能改，完整性破；他在双方面前都冒充对方，认证也破。三条是同一个位置带来的三种能力。

title.en: Cloudflare: an attack that concerns only availability
title.zh: Cloudflare：只关乎可用性的攻击

text.en: In 2025, Cloudflare fended off a **distributed denial of service** (DDoS) attack with a throughput of 31.4 Tbps, coming from a **botnet** made up of millions of compromised devices. A DDoS has just one aim: to exhaust the system's resources so it can no longer serve others.
text.zh: 2025 年，Cloudflare 挡下了一次吞吐量 31.4 Tbps 的**分布式拒绝服务** (distributed denial of service, DDoS) 攻击，攻击来自数百万台被控制的设备组成的**僵尸网络** (botnet)。DDoS 的目的只有一个：把系统的资源耗尽，让它没法再服务别人。

text.en: “Distributed” means the traffic pours in from many devices at once. Why use millions of them? First, the sources are so many and so scattered that no single address can be simply blocked; second, the traffic adds up to something staggering. How big is 31.4 Tbps? A 100 Mbit/s home broadband line is $10^8$ bits per second, and 31.4 Tbps is $3.14\times 10^{13}$; dividing one by the other gives about $3.14\times10^{5}$: the equivalent of over 300,000 home broadband lines all running flat out at one target.
text.zh: “分布式”就是流量从很多台设备同时涌来。为什么要动用数百万台？一是来源太多太散，没有哪个地址能简单地拉黑；二是流量加起来大得惊人。31.4 Tbps 有多大？一条 100 Mbit/s 的家庭宽带是 $10^8$ 比特每秒，31.4 Tbps 是 $3.14\times 10^{13}$，两者相除约 $3.14\times10^{5}$：相当于三十多万条家庭宽带同时满载往一个目标灌。

text.en: Compare with the previous page: this attack looked at no content, changed no data and impersonated nobody; it simply made the service unusable. It concerns only **availability**, and the cost is economic loss.
text.zh: 对照上一页：这次攻击没有偷看任何内容，没有改任何数据，也没有冒充谁，只是让服务用不了。它只关乎**可用性**，代价是经济上的损失。

title.en: What did each of these two hurt?
title.zh: 这两件事各伤到什么

prompt.en: Which properties did each of the following two events break? A: an attacker sits between a student and the course selection website and relays all the data in both directions: he reads the student's password, alters the course number in the selection request before forwarding it to the website, and also pretends to be the website to the student and the student to the website. B: the moment course selection opens, several hundred thousand compromised devices send requests to the course selection website at once, the website will not open, and no data is read or changed.
prompt.zh: 下面两件事，各破坏了哪些性质？甲：攻击者坐在学生和选课网站之间，转手双方的所有数据：他读到了学生的密码，把选课请求里的课号改掉再转给网站，还对学生装作是网站、对网站装作是学生。乙：选课开放的那一刻，几十万台被控制的设备同时向选课网站发请求，网站打不开了，没有任何数据被读或被改。

label.en: A: confidentiality, integrity, authentication; B: availability
label.zh: 甲：机密性、完整性、认证；乙：可用性

feedback.en: Right. A's position brings the three abilities of reading, changing and impersonating; B touched not one byte of content and just exhausted the service.
feedback.zh: 对。甲的位置带来读、改、冒充三种能力；乙一个字节的内容也没碰，只是把服务耗尽。

label.en: A: only confidentiality; B: availability and confidentiality
label.zh: 甲：只有机密性；乙：可用性和机密性

feedback.en: A did more than read: it also changed the course number (integrity) and impersonated the other side (authentication). In B no content was seen, so confidentiality is fine.
feedback.zh: 甲不止读了，还改了课号（完整性），还冒充了对方（认证）。乙里没有任何内容被看到，机密性没事。

label.en: A: availability; B: confidentiality, integrity, authentication
label.zh: 甲：可用性；乙：机密性、完整性、认证

feedback.en: That is backwards. In A the website stays usable throughout, it is just that the person handling the traffic cannot be trusted; B is the one where the service is knocked out.
feedback.zh: 反了。甲里网站一直能用，只是经手的人不可信；乙才是服务被弄瘫。

label.en: Both only break availability, because the victim in both is the course selection website
label.zh: 两件事都只破坏可用性，因为受害的都是选课网站

feedback.en: What matters is not who the victim is but what the attack did: A reads, changes and impersonates, while B only exhausts resources.
feedback.zh: 看的不是受害者是谁，而是攻击做了什么：甲在读、改、冒充，乙只是耗尽资源。

explain.en: Break an attack down by “what it did”: reading hurts confidentiality; changing hurts integrity; impersonating hurts authentication; exhausting resources hurts availability. The man in the middle covers three from a single position, while DDoS covers only one.
explain.zh: 把攻击拆成“它做了什么”：读，伤机密性；改，伤完整性；冒充，伤认证；耗尽资源，伤可用性。中间人一个位置占了三样，DDoS 只占一样。

title.en: Every layer has security measures
title.zh: 每一层都有安全措施

text.en: Security is not the business of any one layer; every layer of the protocol stack has its own line of defence. Think of the five layers that click went through:
text.zh: 安全不是某一层的事，协议栈每一层都有自己的一道防线。想想那次点击走过的五层：

rows.en: Seal the transmission line to prevent wiretapping
rows.zh: 把传输线封起来，防止搭线窃听

text.en: Most of them are built on two things: **cryptography** and **authentication**. So next we study cryptography first.
text.zh: 它们大多建立在两样东西之上：**密码学**和**认证**。所以接下来先学密码学。

title.en: The encryption model: plaintext, ciphertext, key
title.zh: 加密模型：明文、密文、密钥

text.en: Cryptography is a family of algorithms for: making secrets, authenticating users, preventing tampering and preventing denial. Start with the most basic one, “making secrets”.
text.zh: 密码学 (cryptography) 是一组算法：造秘密、认证用户、防篡改、防抵赖。先看最基本的“造秘密”。

alt.en: Alice turns plaintext into ciphertext with encryption method E and key K, and Bob restores it with decryption method D and key K; the intruder Trudy sits in the middle, a passive one only listening and an active one also able to change
alt.zh: Alice 用加密方法 E 和密钥 K 把明文变成密文，Bob 用解密方法 D 和密钥 K 还原；入侵者 Trudy 在中间，被动的只听，主动的还能改

text.en: Alice gives the **plaintext** P to the encryption method E, which is controlled by the **key** K, and it outputs the **ciphertext** C. Bob restores it with the decryption method D and the key. As formulas:
text.zh: Alice 把**明文** (plaintext) P 交给加密方法 E，E 由**密钥** (key) K 控制，输出**密文** (ciphertext) C。Bob 用解密方法 D 和密钥还原。写成式子：

blocks.tex: C = E_K(P),\qquad P = D_K(C),\qquad D_K\bigl(E_K(P)\bigr) = P

text.en: The key is a string of bits, whose role is to pick one way of encrypting out of many possible ones. Trudy in the middle comes in two kinds:
text.zh: 密钥是一串比特，作用是在许多种可能的加密方式里挑出一种。中间的 Trudy 有两种：

items.en: A **passive intruder** only eavesdrops, and directly threatens confidentiality.
items.zh: **被动入侵者**只偷听，直接威胁机密性。

items.en: An **active intruder** can also change messages, which breaks integrity (and may impersonate, affecting authentication).
items.zh: **主动入侵者**还能改消息，会破坏完整性（还可能冒充，影响认证）。

text.en: In the example at the start, “changed without being read”, the attacker is an active intruder.
text.zh: 刚才开头那个“读不懂也能改”的例子，攻击者就是主动入侵者。

title.en: Copy it, or change a few bits?
title.zh: 抄一份，还是改几位

prompt.en: Trudy sits on the line between Alice and Bob and does not know the key. Case A: she makes a copy of every ciphertext and then lets it through unchanged. Case B: she flips a few bits in the ciphertext and then lets it through. In the two cases, what kind of intruder is Trudy?
prompt.zh: Trudy 守在 Alice 和 Bob 的线路上，不知道密钥。情形甲：她把每条密文原样抄一份，再原样放行。情形乙：她把密文里的几位翻转，再放行。两种情形里，Trudy 各算哪一种入侵者？

label.en: A is a passive intruder, B is an active intruder
label.zh: 甲是被动入侵者，乙是主动入侵者

feedback.en: Right. Copying and leaving the message untouched is passive, threatening only confidentiality; changing the message is active and breaks integrity. In B, even if she cannot read it, she can change it.
feedback.zh: 对。抄一份、不动消息是被动，只威胁机密性；改了消息就是主动，破坏完整性。乙里她就算读不懂，也能改。

label.en: A is an active intruder, B is a passive intruder
label.zh: 甲是主动入侵者，乙是被动入侵者

feedback.en: That is reversed. What counts is whether the message is changed: only listening without touching it is passive, and acting to change it is active.
feedback.zh: 颠倒了。看有没有改动消息：只听不动是被动，动手改才是主动。

label.en: Both are passive, because she has no key and can do nothing
label.zh: 两种都是被动，因为她没有密钥，什么也做不了

feedback.en: Having no key only means she cannot read it; it does not mean she can do nothing. In the transfer example at the start, she could change it without reading it. Encryption covers only confidentiality.
feedback.zh: 没有密钥只是读不懂，不等于什么也做不了：开头那个转账的例子里，读不懂照样能改。加密只管机密性。

label.en: Both are active, because in both she touched the line
label.zh: 两种都是主动，因为她都碰了线路

feedback.en: Touching the line does not count; what counts is whether the message is changed. Copying it and letting it through unchanged leaves the message as it was, so she is still passive.
feedback.zh: 碰线路不算，算的是有没有改变消息。抄一份再原样放行，消息没变，仍是被动。

explain.en: The dividing line between passive and active is “whether the message is changed”. Encryption stops a passive intruder reading, which covers confidentiality; but it cannot stop an active intruder changing messages, so integrity needs another approach.
explain.zh: 被动和主动的分界线是“改不改消息”。加密让被动入侵者读不懂，管得了机密性；可它拦不住主动入侵者改消息，完整性要另想办法。

title.en: Kerckhoffs's principle: the algorithm is public, only the key is secret
title.zh: 柯克霍夫原则：算法公开，只有密钥保密

text.en: **Kerckhoffs's principle**: the encryption and decryption algorithms E and D are public, and only the key K is secret. This sounds counterintuitive: why not hide the algorithm too, which would be safer?
text.zh: **柯克霍夫原则** (Kerckhoff's principle)：加密和解密的算法 E、D 是公开的，只有密钥 K 是秘密。这听着反直觉：为什么不连算法也藏起来，不是更保险吗？

items.en: **Only what is public can stand up to scrutiny.** People all over the world look for flaws, and only when none is found is there reason to trust it. A hidden algorithm has been looked at only by its designer.
items.zh: **公开才经得起检验。** 全世界的人都来找漏洞，没找出问题，才有理由信它。藏起来的算法，只有设计者自己看过。

items.en: **A leaked algorithm cannot be taken back, but a key can be changed.** The algorithm is used by the whole system, and once it leaks, everyone has to start over; when a key leaks, you just change to another, and you can change it at any time.
items.zh: **算法泄露就收不回来，密钥可以换。** 算法是整个系统都在用的，一旦泄露，只能全体重做；密钥一泄露，换一把就行，也可以随时换。

text.en: The slides also have a requirement: in a simple cryptosystem, decryption restores the plaintext if and only if encryption and decryption use the same key: $D_{K_2}(E_{K_1}(P)) = P$ holds if and only if $K_1 = K_2$.
text.zh: 课件里还有一条要求：简单的密码系统里，解密能还原明文，当且仅当加密和解密用的是同一把钥匙：$D_{K_2}(E_{K_1}(P)) = P$ 成立，当且仅当 $K_1 = K_2$。

title.en: True only for symmetric keys
title.zh: 只对对称密钥成立

body.en: “If and only if the two keys are the same” is correct only when encryption and decryption use one and the same key. The public-key cryptography in the next lesson uses two different keys and still restores the plaintext, so do not treat this as a general rule.
body.zh: “当且仅当两把钥匙一样”只在加密、解密同用一把钥匙时才对。下一课的公钥密码会用两把不同的钥匙，却依然能还原，所以不要把它当成通用规则。

title.en: A secret algorithm
title.zh: 保密的算法

prompt.en: A company advertises: “Our encryption algorithm was designed in-house and has never been made public, so hackers cannot break it.” By Kerckhoffs's principle, what should worry you most about this claim?
prompt.zh: 一家公司宣传：“我们的加密算法是自己设计的，从不公开，所以黑客没法破。”按柯克霍夫原则，你对这句话最该担心什么？

label.en: The algorithm has not been publicly scrutinised, and once it leaks, the whole system has to be redone
label.zh: 算法没经过公开检验，一旦泄露，整个系统只能整体重做

feedback.en: Right. Being public lets more people look for flaws; a secret algorithm that leaks cannot be taken back, and cannot be swapped out the way a key can.
feedback.zh: 对。公开让更多人来找漏洞；保密的算法一旦泄露，收不回来，也没法像换密钥那样换掉。

label.en: Nothing to worry about; a secret algorithm is secure enough
label.zh: 没什么可担心的，算法保密就足够安全了

feedback.en: Security cannot be staked on keeping the algorithm secret: only its designer has examined it, and if it leaks, everything is lost.
feedback.zh: 安全不能押在算法保密上：它只有设计者看过，一旦泄露就是全盘皆输。

label.en: A secret algorithm is certainly weaker than a public one
label.zh: 保密的算法一定比公开的弱

feedback.en: It is not “certainly weak”, but “nobody has checked it, so we do not know whether it is strong”. A public algorithm has been checked again and again, and that is what gives reason to trust it.
feedback.zh: 不是“一定弱”，而是“没人检验过，不知道强不强”。公开的算法被反复检验过，才有理由信它。

label.en: The key should be made public too, to be fair
label.zh: 应该把密钥也一起公开，这样才公平

feedback.en: The key is the part that must be kept secret. In a system like this that shares one key, once the key is public, anyone can decrypt.
feedback.zh: 密钥才是必须保密的那一部分。在这种共用一把密钥的系统里，密钥一公开，谁都能解密。

explain.en: Kerckhoffs's principle concentrates the secret in the key: the algorithm is public and open to scrutiny, and the key can be replaced at any time. Staking the security of the whole system on “nobody knows the algorithm” means one leak ends it all.
explain.zh: 柯克霍夫原则把秘密集中在密钥上：算法公开、接受检验，密钥可以随时更换。把整个系统的安全押在“没人知道算法”上，泄露一次就全完。

title.en: Key space: each extra bit doubles the work
title.zh: 密钥空间：每多一位，工作量翻倍

intro.en: Since everyone knows the algorithm, the dumbest thing an attacker can do is try every possible key one by one (brute-force search). A key has n bits, each bit is 0 or 1, so there are $2^n$ possible keys in all, called the **key space**.
intro.zh: 既然算法人人知道，攻击者最笨的办法就是把所有可能的密钥挨个试一遍（暴力搜索）。密钥有 n 位，每一位是 0 或 1，所以一共有 $2^n$ 种密钥，这叫**密钥空间** (key space)。

lines.tex: n\text{ 位密钥} \Rightarrow 2^n \text{ 种可能}

why.en: Each bit has two choices, so each extra bit multiplies the total by 2
why.zh: 每一位两种选择，位数每多一位，总数乘 2

why.en: One more bit than 56 doubles the work of brute-force search
why.zh: 56 位多一位，暴力搜索的工作量就翻倍

why.en: The key space of a 128-bit key is $2^{72}$ times larger than that of a 56-bit key
why.zh: 128 位的密钥空间比 56 位大 $2^{72}$ 倍
约四十七万亿亿倍（一万亿亿是 $10^{20}$）

why.en: To get a feel for it, suppose the attacker has a machine that tries a billion keys per second (this number is assumed, used only to get a sense of scale). For a 40-bit key, trying every possibility in the worst case takes only a dozen or so minutes
why.zh: 为了有个体感，假设攻击者有一台每秒试 10 亿把密钥的机器（这个数是假设的，只用来感受量级）。40 位的密钥，最坏试遍所有可能，十几分钟就够

why.en: With 16 more bits, the work is $2^{16}=65536$ times as much, going from a dozen or so minutes to over two years
why.zh: 多了 16 位，工作量是 $2^{16}=65536$ 倍，从十几分钟变成两年多

why.en: With 128 bits: the universe so far is only about $1.4\times 10^{10}$ years old, so this is over a dozen orders of magnitude more
why.zh: 128 位：宇宙至今才约 $1.4\times 10^{10}$ 年，差了十几个数量级

outro.en: So a longer key is harder to break, and exponentially harder: each extra bit doubles it, and 8 more bits is 256 times. This is also why “public algorithm, secret key” can be relied on: the security rests on a long string of random bits.
outro.zh: 所以密钥越长越难破，而且是指数式地难：每多一位翻倍，多 8 位就是 256 倍。这也是“算法公开、密钥保密”靠得住的原因：安全放在一串很长的随机比特上。

title.en: How long for 8 more bits?
title.zh: 多 8 位要多久

prompt.en: We calculated just now: a machine that tries a billion keys per second takes about 1100 seconds in the worst case to search a 40-bit key. How many seconds does the same machine need, in the worst case, to search a 48-bit key?
prompt.zh: 刚才算过：一台每秒试 10 亿把密钥的机器，搜 40 位密钥最坏要约 1100 秒。同一台机器搜 48 位的密钥，最坏大约要多少秒？

hints.en: 48 bits is 8 more than 40. By what factor does each extra bit multiply the work?
hints.zh: 48 位比 40 位多 8 位。每多一位，工作量乘几？

explain.en: With 8 more bits, the work is $2^8 = 256$ times as much: 1100 × 256 is about 280,000 seconds, about 3.3 days. The bit count went up only a little, yet the time has risen from a dozen or so minutes to several days; go up to 56 bits and it is over two years.
explain.zh: 多 8 位，工作量是 $2^8 = 256$ 倍：1100 × 256 约 28 万秒，约 3.3 天。位数只加了一点，时间已经从十几分钟涨到好几天；再加到 56 位就是两年多。

title.en: The simplest cipher: move each letter along a few places
title.zh: 最简单的密码：每个字母往后挪几位

text.en: The simplest encryption: replace each letter with the K-th letter after it in the alphabet, wrapping from z round to a. K is the key.
text.zh: 最简单的加密：把每个字母换成字母表里往后第 K 个，z 之后绕回 a。K 就是密钥。

items.en: K = 1: where becomes xifsf (w to x, h to i, e to f, r to s, e to f).
items.zh: K = 1：where 变成 xifsf（w 到 x，h 到 i，e 到 f，r 到 s，e 到 f）。

items.en: K = 4: a becomes e, z becomes d; where becomes alivi.
items.zh: K = 4：a 变成 e，z 变成 d；where 变成 alivi。

text.en: Decryption just moves back the other way. But this cipher is extremely easy to break: the key has only the twenty-odd values 1 to 25 (shifting by 0 is no encryption at all, and shifting by 26 returns to the original). An attacker who gets the ciphertext alivi shifts back one place at a time:
text.zh: 解密就是倒着挪回来。可这个密码极易破：密钥只有 1 到 25 这二十几种（挪 0 位等于没加密，挪 26 位又回到原样）。攻击者拿到密文 alivi，挨个往回挪：

text.en: The first three are not words, and the fourth is, so that is it. At most 25 tries. With the key space this small, even the best algorithm is no use.
text.zh: 前三个不是单词，第四个是，就是它了。最多试 25 次。密钥空间太小，再好的算法也没用。

title.en: Substitution ciphers: any lookup table can still be broken
title.zh: 替换密码：任意对照表，也能被破

text.en: A **substitution cipher** systematically replaces each letter (or group of letters) with something else. It need not shift every letter by the same number; it can use any lookup table, for example replacing letters in the order of the keyboard's QWERTY layout:
text.zh: **替换密码** (substitution cipher) 把每个字母（或几个字母）系统地换成别的。不必每个都挪同样的位数，可以用任意一张对照表，比如把字母换成键盘 QWERTY 的顺序：

blocks.code:
明文  a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z
密文  Q W E R T Y U I O P A S D F G H J K L Z X C V B N M

text.en: You receive the ciphertext were; what is the plaintext? Look it up backwards in the table: W is the ciphertext of b, E is c, R is d, E is c, so the plaintext is **bcdc**.
text.zh: 收到密文 were，明文是什么？对着表倒查：W 是 b 的密文，E 是 c，R 是 d，E 是 c，所以明文是 **bcdc**。

text.en: This table can be arranged in $26!\approx 4\times10^{26}$ ways, and brute-force search is impractical. Yet it can still be broken, not by trying but by **statistics**: the cryptanalyst uses the statistical features of natural language. In English e is the most common letter, so the most frequent letter in the ciphertext is very likely e; then looking at common words and letter combinations, the whole table is guessed bit by bit. Each letter has changed its look, but the **frequency** with which it appears has not.
text.zh: 这张表一共有 $26!\approx 4\times10^{26}$ 种排法，暴力搜索不现实。可它还是能被破，办法不是试，而是**统计**：密码分析者 (cryptanalyst) 利用自然语言的统计特征。英语里 e 最常见，密文里出现最多的那个字母很可能就是 e；再看常见的单词和字母搭配，一点点猜出整张表。每个字母换了模样，但它出现的**频率**没变。

title.en: K is the most common in the ciphertext
title.zh: 密文里 K 最多

prompt.en: You intercept a long piece of English ciphertext produced with an arbitrary lookup table, and you do not have the key. Counting, the letter K appears the most, making up about 12% of all letters. What is the most reasonable guess?
prompt.zh: 截获一大段英文密文，用的是一张任意的对照表，你没有密钥。数一数，字母 K 出现得最多，约占全部字母的 12%。最合理的猜测是什么？

label.en: K is most likely the ciphertext of e
label.zh: K 多半是 e 的密文

feedback.en: Right. In English e is the most common letter, about 12% to 13%. The letters changed their look, but their frequency did not.
feedback.zh: 对。英语里 e 最常见，约占 12% 到 13%。字母换了模样，出现的频率却没变。

label.en: K is most likely the ciphertext of k
label.zh: K 多半是 k 的密文

feedback.en: A substitution cipher replaces letters with other letters, and there is no reason for one to stay the same after replacement.
feedback.zh: 替换密码就是把字母换成别的字母，没有理由换了以后还是原来那个。

label.en: It cannot be guessed: the table is arbitrary, with 26! possibilities, and you can only try them one by one
label.zh: 没法猜：表是任意排的，有 26! 种，只能一个个试

feedback.en: Trying them one by one is indeed impractical, but statistics give a clue, so there is no need to try. A large key space does not mean it cannot be broken.
feedback.zh: 一个个试确实不现实，可统计给了线索，不用试。密钥空间大，不等于破不了。

label.en: K is most likely the ciphertext of z
label.zh: K 多半是 z 的密文

feedback.en: z is one of the rarest letters in English, so it cannot be the most common one.
feedback.zh: z 是英语里最罕见的字母之一，出现最多的不会是它。

explain.en: A substitution cipher changes the look of the letters but not how often they appear. So the analyst first counts frequencies, then combines them with common words and letter combinations to guess the whole table step by step, with no need to try 26! possibilities. A transposition cipher is the opposite: not one letter is changed, the frequencies stay as they were, and frequency analysis is no help; the attacker faces a puzzle of order.
explain.zh: 替换密码换掉的是字母的模样，没换它出现的频率。所以分析者先数频率，再结合常见单词和搭配，一步步猜出整张表，不用试 26! 种。换位密码正相反：字母一个没换，频率原样，频率分析帮不上忙，攻击者面对的是顺序的谜。

title.en: Transposition ciphers: the letters stay, only the order is scrambled
title.zh: 换位密码：字母不变，只乱顺序

text.en: A **transposition cipher** is the opposite of substitution: not one letter is changed, only their order is scrambled. The slides use the keyword MEGABUCK as the key:
text.zh: **换位密码** (transposition cipher) 和替换相反：一个字母都不改，只把它们的顺序打乱。课件用关键词 MEGABUCK 做密钥：

items.en: Write the plaintext into a table, row by row, with as many columns as the keyword has letters (8 columns).
items.zh: 把明文按关键词的列数（8 列）一行行写成表。

items.en: Number the columns by the alphabetical order of the keyword's letters: A is 1, B is 2, C is 3, E is 4, G is 5, K is 6, M is 7, U is 8.
items.zh: 按关键词字母的字母顺序给各列编号：A 是 1，B 是 2，C 是 3，E 是 4，G 是 5，K 是 6，M 是 7，U 是 8。

items.en: Read the columns off one at a time in the order of the numbers 1, 2, 3 and so on, and that is the ciphertext.
items.zh: 按编号 1、2、3……的顺序，一列一列读下来，就是密文。

items.en: If the last row of plaintext is short, pad it out with abcd.
items.zh: 明文最后一行不满时，用 abcd 补满。

text.en: Column 1 (A) read from top to bottom is AFLLSKSO, column 2 (B) is SELAWAIA, column 3 (C) is TOOSSCTC... reading all eight columns in turn, the whole ciphertext is:
text.zh: 第 1 列（A）从上往下读是 AFLLSKSO，第 2 列（B）是 SELAWAIA，第 3 列（C）是 TOOSSCTC……八列依次读完，整条密文是：

blocks.code: AFLLSKSO SELAWAIA TOOSSCTC LNMOMANT ESILYNTW RNNTSOWD PAEDOBUO ERIRICXB

caption.en: The complete ciphertext: eight segments are eight columns (the spaces are only to show the segments clearly; the real ciphertext runs together)
caption.zh: 完整密文：八段就是八列（空格只是为了看清分段，真正的密文连在一起）

text.en: Why pad it out? Because the recipient has only one long run of ciphertext, and once it is padded every column is the same length (here, 8 letters each), so he knows that a column boundary falls every 8 letters. Decryption goes the other way: cut the ciphertext into eight segments by column length, put them back into the columns by number, and read row by row.
text.zh: 为什么要补满？因为收信人只有一长串密文，补满后每一列一样长（这里都是 8 个字母），他才知道每隔 8 个字母就是一列的分界。解密反过来：按列长把密文切成八段，按编号放回各列，再一行行读。

text.en: Why does scrambling the positions hide the meaning? Not one letter is missing, but “which letter is in which column and which row” is all mixed up. What the attacker lacks is exactly the order of the columns, which is the key. Also, a transposition cipher does not change the letters, so the letter frequency distribution looks exactly like normal language, which is where it differs from a substitution cipher.
text.zh: 打乱位置为什么就藏住了意思？字母一个没少，可“哪个字母在哪一列、第几行”全乱了。攻击者缺的恰好是列的顺序，也就是密钥。另外，换位密码不改字母，所以字母的频率分布看起来和正常语言一模一样，这是它和替换密码不同的地方。

title.en: Transpose one yourself
title.zh: 自己换一次位

prompt.en: Use the keyword CAB for a transposition cipher, with the plaintext meetnow, padded with ab at the end to make meetnowab. After writing it into a table with 3 columns, what is the ciphertext?
prompt.zh: 用关键词 CAB 做换位密码，明文 meetnow，末尾用 ab 补满成 meetnowab。按 3 列写成表后，密文是什么？

feedback.en: Right. The three columns are column C mtw, column A ena, column B eob; read in the order A, B, C, that gives ena, eob, mtw.
feedback.zh: 对。三列分别是 C 列 mtw、A 列 ena、B 列 eob；按 A、B、C 的次序读就是 ena、eob、mtw。

feedback.en: That reads the columns left to right. You have to read them in the alphabetical order of the keyword's letters (A, B, C).
feedback.zh: 这是从左到右读列。要按关键词字母的字母顺序（A、B、C）读。

feedback.en: That is the original text, read row by row, with no transposition.
feedback.zh: 这是原文，一行行读，没有换位。

hints.en: First write it as three rows: mee, tno, wab. The three columns from left to right correspond to the keyword's C, A, B.
hints.zh: 先写成三行：mee、tno、wab。三列从左到右分别对应关键词的 C、A、B。

explain.en: A is 1st, B is 2nd, C is 3rd. So first read column A (the second column) ena, then column B (the third column) eob, and last column C (the first column) mtw.
explain.zh: A 是第 1 个，B 是第 2 个，C 是第 3 个。所以先读 A 列（第二列）ena，再读 B 列（第三列）eob，最后读 C 列（第一列）mtw。

title.en: XOR: an operation that undoes itself
title.zh: 异或：一个自己能还原自己的运算

text.en: The last cipher uses **exclusive or** (XOR). It means “A or B, but not both”: two equal bits give 0, two different bits give 1.
text.zh: 最后一个密码要用**异或** (XOR)。它的意思是“A 或 B，但不能都是”：两位相同得 0，不同得 1。

text.en: Take A as the data and B as the key, and see what happens:
text.zh: 把 A 当成数据，B 当成密钥，看会发生什么：

head.zh: 密文（数据 XOR 密钥）
接收方还原（密文 XOR 密钥）

text.en: The last column is exactly the same as the first. XORing with the same key twice brings you back to the start. Why? Because any number XORed with itself gives 0, and XOR with 0 changes nothing.
text.zh: 最后一列和第一列完全相同。同一把密钥异或两次，就回到原来。为什么？因为任何数和自己异或得 0，再和 0 异或不变。

title.en: The one-time pad: work it through
title.zh: 一次性密码本：算一遍

intro.en: The method of the **one-time pad**: first turn the plaintext into a string of bits (for example by taking its ASCII), use a string of **random** bits as the key, and XOR them bit by bit to get the ciphertext. To decrypt, XOR bit by bit with the same key string again. We work it with the slides' data: plaintext 00110101, key 11100011.
intro.zh: **一次性密码本** (one-time pad) 的做法：先把明文转成比特串（比如取它的 ASCII），用一串**随机**比特做密钥，逐位异或得到密文。解密时，再与同一串密钥逐位异或。我们按课件的数据算：明文 00110101，密钥 11100011。

why.en: Encrypt. Bit by bit: 0 and 1 give 1, 0 and 1 give 1, 1 and 1 give 0, 1 and 0 give 1, 0 and 0 give 0, 1 and 0 give 1, 0 and 1 give 1, 1 and 1 give 0
Decrypt. XOR once more with the same key string, and working bit by bit gives exactly the original plaintext
why.zh: 解密。用同一串密钥再异或一次，逐位算下来，正好是原来的明文

lines.tex: (P\oplus K)\oplus K = P\oplus (K\oplus K) = P\oplus 0 = P

why.en: Why it works every time: K XORed with itself gives 0, and P XORed with 0 is unchanged
why.zh: 为什么每次都行：K 与自己异或得 0，P 与 0 异或不变

outro.en: Encryption and decryption are the same operation, and this is what symmetric means: both sides hold the same key string.
outro.zh: 加密和解密是同一个操作，这就是对称：双方拥有同一串密钥。

title.en: XOR by hand
title.zh: 异或手算

prompt.en: The ASCII of the letter h is 01101000, and the one-time pad key is 10110101. Encrypting with XOR, what is the ciphertext?
prompt.zh: 字母 h 的 ASCII 是 01101000，一次性密码本的密钥是 10110101。用异或加密，密文是什么？

feedback.en: Right. Bit by bit: 0 and 1 give 1, 1 and 0 give 1, 1 and 1 give 0, 0 and 1 give 1, 1 and 0 give 1, 0 and 1 give 1, 0 and 0 give 0, 0 and 1 give 1.
This is the bitwise “or”: it also gives 1 when both bits are 1. XOR requires two equal bits to give 0, so the third bit should be 0.
feedback.zh: 这是逐位“或”的结果：两位都是 1 时也得 1。异或要求两位相同得 0，所以第三位应是 0。

feedback.en: This is the bitwise “and”, which gives 1 only when both bits are 1. It loses information and cannot be restored with the key.
feedback.zh: 这是逐位“与”的结果，只有两位都是 1 才得 1。它丢了信息，没法用密钥还原。

explain.en: XOR has just one rule: equal gives 0, different gives 1. XORing 11011101 with the same string 10110101 again returns 01101000, which is h.
explain.zh: 异或的规则只有一条：相同得 0，不同得 1。用同一串 10110101 再异或 11011101，就会回到 01101000，也就是 h。

title.en: Why it is harder to break, and why it is hard to use
title.zh: 为什么更难破，又为什么难用

text.en: The one-time pad is harder to break in the sense of information theory: as long as the key is truly random, as long as the plaintext, and used only once, an attacker looking at the ciphertext has no clue whatsoever. For example, the ciphertext 11010110 could come from plaintext 00110101 with key 11100011, or from 00000000 with key 11010110. There is no way to judge which is the true one.
text.zh: 一次性密码本在信息论的意义上更难破：只要密钥是真随机的、和明文一样长、只用一次，攻击者看着密文，没有任何线索。例如密文是 11010110，既可能来自明文 00110101 加密钥 11100011，也可能来自 00000000 加密钥 11010110。哪一个才是真的，没有办法判断。

text.en: The drawbacks are also plain:
text.zh: 缺点也很明显：

items.en: **The key cannot be memorised**: it is a long string of random bits that must be carried around.
items.zh: **密钥记不住**：它是一长串随机比特，得带着。

items.en: **The total amount of data that can be sent is limited by the amount of key**: a key can be used only once, so sending any amount of data takes that much key.
items.zh: **能传的数据总量受密钥量限制**：密钥只能用一次，传多少数据就要有多少密钥。

items.en: **It is very sensitive to lost or inserted characters**: lose one bit and everything after it is shifted out of place and all decrypted wrongly.
items.zh: **对丢失或插入的字符很敏感**：丢一位，后面所有位都错位，全部解错。

title.en: Beyond the slides: why the key must never be reused
title.zh: 超出课件：为什么密钥绝不能重复用

body.en: If two messages use the same key K, the attacker XORs the two ciphertexts: $(P_1\oplus K)\oplus(P_2\oplus K) = P_1\oplus P_2$, K cancels, leaving the XOR of the two plaintexts, and information about the plaintexts leaks. The “keystream reuse attack” in the next lesson uses exactly this.
body.zh: 如果两条消息用了同一把密钥 K，攻击者把两条密文异或：$(P_1\oplus K)\oplus(P_2\oplus K) = P_1\oplus P_2$，K 抵消了，剩下两条明文的异或，明文的信息就漏了。下一课的“密钥流重用攻击”用的正是这一点。
